note: Rules checked against public sources on 2026-11-14. Items marked verify:true must be re-checked against the live EPFO portal before telling a user.

reasons.title: KYC not verified / Aadhaar not linked to UAN
reasons.plain: EPFO can't confirm who you are because your Aadhaar, PAN or bank details are not verified on your PF account.
steps: Log in to the EPFO Member Portal (unifiedportal-mem.epfindia.gov.in) with your UAN.
Go to Manage → KYC and check Aadhaar, PAN and Bank. All three should show 'Verified'.
If anything is 'Pending', ask your current or last employer's HR to approve it (they approve KYC on their side).
If Aadhaar is not linked, link it under Manage → KYC using Aadhaar OTP.
Wait 2–7 days for the status to show 'Verified', then file the claim again.

reasons.title: Name doesn't match Aadhaar / PAN / bank
reasons.plain: The spelling or order of your name on PF records is different from your Aadhaar, PAN or bank account. Even a missing middle name or initial can cause this.
reasons.who_fixes: member (online if Aadhaar-verified), else member + employer
steps: Compare your name exactly across: PF profile, Aadhaar, PAN and bank account.
If your UAN is Aadhaar-verified: Member Portal → Manage → Joint Declaration / Modify Basic Details, and correct the name to match Aadhaar.
If your UAN is NOT Aadhaar-verified: fill the Joint Declaration form with your employer and submit with proof (Aadhaar, PAN, passport etc.).
If your bank account name is the one that's different, get the bank to correct it first, then update bank KYC on the portal.
Once the correction shows on your profile, file the claim again.
documents: Any one more ID: passport / driving licence / school certificate

reasons.title: Date of birth doesn't match
reasons.plain: Your date of birth on PF records is different from your Aadhaar. Often the employer typed it wrong when you joined.
reasons.who_fixes: member (online if Aadhaar-verified), else member + employer
steps: Check your DOB on the PF profile vs Aadhaar.
Aadhaar-verified UAN: correct it online via Joint Declaration / Modify Basic Details.
Not Aadhaar-verified: Joint Declaration through employer with DOB proof (birth certificate, school leaving certificate, passport).
File the claim again after the corrected DOB shows on your profile.
documents: Birth certificate or school leaving certificate or passport

reasons.title: Bank account problem
reasons.plain: The bank account linked to your PF is wrong, closed, inactive, or not verified, so EPFO can't send money to it.
steps: Make sure the account is active and in your own name (not joint as secondary holder).
Member Portal → Manage → KYC → add or update the bank account with the correct IFSC.
Ask your employer to approve the new bank KYC.
Wait for 'Verified', then file again.
documents: Bank passbook first page or cancelled cheque showing your name, account number and IFSC

reasons.title: Cheque / passbook image unclear
reasons.plain: The cheque or passbook photo you uploaded was blurry, or didn't clearly show your name, account number and IFSC.
steps: Take a fresh, clear photo of a cancelled cheque or passbook front page in good light.
Your printed name, account number and IFSC must all be clearly readable.
If your cheque doesn't have your name printed, use the passbook page instead, or get a personalised cheque book.
File the claim again and upload the new image.
documents: Cancelled cheque with printed name, or passbook front page

reasons.title: Date of exit not updated
reasons.plain: EPFO still thinks you're working at your old company, so you can't do a final withdrawal from that account.
reasons.who_fixes: employer, or member (after 2 months with no contribution)
steps: Ask your old employer's HR to mark your date of exit on the employer portal.
If they don't respond: once 2 months have passed since the last PF contribution, you can mark it yourself — Member Portal → Manage → Mark Exit.
Pick the correct reason for leaving and verify with Aadhaar OTP.
After the exit date shows, file the claim again.

reasons.title: Not eligible — service period / waiting period
reasons.plain: EPFO thinks you haven't worked long enough, or haven't waited long enough after leaving, for the type of withdrawal you asked for.
steps: Check your total service in the passbook. Old jobs that were never transferred may not be counted — transfer them first (see 'Multiple UANs / transfer pending').
Check the current rules: after the Oct 2025 changes, partial withdrawals need 12 months of service, and full settlement and pension (EPS) withdrawal have longer waiting periods after leaving a job.
If you truly were eligible (e.g. 10 years of service but rejected as 'insufficient'), this is likely an EPFO error: raise an EPFiGMS grievance with your passbook as proof.
If you're not yet eligible, choose a withdrawal type you ARE eligible for (e.g. partial withdrawal) instead.
documents: EPF passbook for all member IDs

reasons.title: Multiple UANs / old PF not transferred
reasons.plain: Your PF from earlier jobs is sitting in a different account or UAN and hasn't been combined, so your service and balance look smaller than they are.
steps: Member Portal → View → Service History, to list all your member IDs.
Online Services → One Member One EPF Account (Transfer Request) to move old balances into the current account.
If you have two UANs, email or raise a grievance to get the old UAN merged/deactivated.
Wait for the transfer to complete, then file the claim again.

reasons.title: EPS contribution on wages above ₹15,000
reasons.plain: Your employer put money into the pension scheme (EPS) when your salary was too high for it. EPFO wants that corrected before paying you.
steps: Ask your employer HR / their PF consultant to submit a request to transfer the wrongly paid EPS amount back into your EPF account.
Once the field office approves it, file the claim again.
If the employer doesn't act within 15 days, raise an EPFiGMS grievance naming the employer.
documents: Salary slips showing basic + DA above ₹15,000

reasons.title: Form 15G / 15H problem
reasons.plain: The tax form you uploaded to avoid TDS was filled wrongly (often the wrong assessment year), or wasn't allowed.
steps: Only upload Form 15G (or 15H if you're 60+) if your total income for the year is below the taxable limit.
Fill the correct financial year and assessment year (assessment year = the year after the financial year).
Make sure PAN is filled. If unsure, skip 15G — TDS will be deducted, which you can claim back in your ITR.
File the claim again.

reasons.title: Employer problem (DSC / approval / company closed)
reasons.plain: Something on your employer's side is blocking the claim — for example they haven't registered their digital signature, haven't approved your request, or the company has shut down.
reasons.who_fixes: employer; if unavailable, EPFO regional office
steps: Email your old employer's HR with your UAN and the rejection reason, asking them to fix it. Keep the email as proof.
If the company has closed or doesn't reply in 15 days, raise an EPFiGMS grievance against the establishment.
For closed companies, the regional EPFO office can process claims with attestation by a bank manager or gazetted officer.
documents: Appointment / relieving letter or salary slips as proof of employment

reasons.title: Wrong form or wrong purpose selected
reasons.plain: You filed the wrong type of claim — for example a final settlement while still employed, or the wrong reason for a partial withdrawal.
steps: Still working? Use partial withdrawal (Form 31) and pick the right category.
Left your job and want everything? Use final settlement (Form 19) for PF, plus Form 10C for pension (EPS) if eligible.
File the claim again with the correct form.

reasons.title: Stuck for weeks or rejected with no clear reason
reasons.plain: Your claim isn't moving, or it was rejected with a vague reason. This needs escalation, not a fix.
steps: If 20+ days have passed since filing, start the escalation ladder below.
Keep: claim ID, filing date, rejection SMS/screenshot, passbook.
